analysis:
Examined three cluster-membership files in provider-swift. None touches the coordinator WebSocket, the Apple attestation chain, App Attest authorization, or the encrypted prefix cache directly, so I found no regression against the retained threat IDs.

1. ClusterApprovalAttachment.swift (head 138-139): the save-time check now calls ClusterConfiguration.validate(capability:rawCapabilitySHA256:) on the setup with the attachment, instead of only ClusterNativeMemberAttachment.validate. This is stricter, and per the comment it also refuses setups that pair an approval with a tensor assistant. Nothing is loosened. I could not see the ClusterConfiguration.validate body, so I assumed it is a superset of the attachment validation and does not skip a previously run check.

2. ClusterApprovalCheck.swift: a `failing` approval is now retried after failingSeconds (3600). The gate at head 134 admits only 0 <= now - setAt < 3600. A missing setAt (older record) or a clock set back (negative delta) therefore falls outside the window and allows retry, which is fail-open, and the retry takes the same build's approval again. The worst outcome is a bounded, hourly retry of an approval that failed. It still passes through ClusterApprovalSync.decision, which re-checks facts and lifetime, so it is availability and flapping behavior and not an authorization bypass. memberQuickEnds (head 152) no longer counts a quick end whose error line matches negotiationFailed. A hostile or flaky coordinator could therefore keep a member from reaching the failing threshold. The effect is a pair that keeps re-registering instead of falling back to local serving. That is a coordinator-side availability matter, and the coordinator is trusted in this model.

3. ClusterOnboardingLive.swift: the serving scope is now forwarded in ClusterControlRequest for planModels and adopt. A forwarded scope from the peer is used to choose whether the plan targets the coordinator (`coordinator: !planningScope(scope).isLocalOnly`). The peer is a paired cluster member. I could not see ClusterControlRequest's authentication or the decoding of `scope`, so I could not confirm that a malicious peer cannot induce a different scope. Its worst-case effect is a plan computed for local-only serving or for the coordinator. Both choices still pass later validation at save time.

Open integration questions: the definition of ClusterConfiguration.validate, the control-channel authentication for forwarded scope, and ClusterService's reset of the quick-end count.
